raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

#3212 fixed FusedAdam's handling of empty tensors: `MultiTensorApply` now drops
zero-numel tensors before launch, and `multi_tensor_apply` rejects them. Its
regression test, `test_empty_param_at_end_of_group`, puts the empty tensor in
slot 2 of a 2-tensor launch. That does not cover the case reported in #3202,
where the empty tensor falls in the last `TensorListMetadata` slot and more
tensors follow. Before #3212, that case wrote past the end of the metadata
arrays.

This adds a test for that exact boundary. It puts the empty tensor in slot 36
(depth-4 Adam) or slot 30 (depth-5 Adam with master weights), follows it with
20 more tensors, and compares against `torch.optim.Adam` over 7 steps. It runs
with and without `capturable`.

Fixes #3202

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

Test-only change.

## Changes

- Add `TestFusedAdam.test_empty_param_in_last_metadata_slot`, parametrized
  over `master_weights` and `capturable`.

## Testing

1x NVIDIA L40 (sm89), driver 570.195.03, CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128,
built in `nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.8.0-devel-ubuntu22.04` with
`NVTE_FRAMEWORK=pytorch NVTE_CUDA_ARCHS=89`.

On this branch, `python -m pytest -v tests/pytorch/test_fused_optimizer.py -k TestFusedAdam`:
31 passed, 4 skipped (MXFP8 and FP8 block-scaling tests that need a newer GPU),
including all four new cases.

On 68493d2d, the commit before #3212, the same check (run as a standalone copy
of the test, because the in-suite version does not apply there) fails in all
four cases:

- `master_weights=False`: parameters come back NaN (silent corruption).
- `master_weights=True`: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`.

This matches the two symptoms described in #3202.

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

Confidence Score: 4/5

**[Low impact]** The change reaches FusedAdam\'s tests\, not its runtime behavior\. The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking test issue that weakens the FP32 checks.

Findings

1.  **FP32 checks compare shared values** ▶

Summary

Adds four regression cases for an empty parameter at the last launch slot, followed by more parameters. - FusedAdam tests cover empty parameters at a launch boundary. Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["Test FusedAdam with an empty param in th..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/fd252f73fd7c3c84c933f927e55874b1c7f07844) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**FP32 checks compare shared values** When `master_weights=False`, `p` is already FP32, so `p.detach().float()` shares its storage instead of copying it. Both optimizers update the same values, and the final comparison checks shared storage against itself. Wrong finite updates or skipped updates can therefore pass in both `capturable` cases. Use `p.detach().clone().float()` to give the reference independent values. ```suggestion ref_params = [torch.nn.Parameter(p.detach().clone().float()) for p in tst_params] ```

detail.title: [PyTorch] Test FusedAdam with an empty param in the last launch slot

files.patch:
@@ -328,6 +328,52 @@ def test_empty_param_at_end_of_group(self):
 
         torch.testing.assert_close(ref_param, tst_param)
 
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("capturable", [False, True])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("master_weights", [False, True])
+    def test_empty_param_in_last_metadata_slot(self, master_weights, capturable):
+        """An empty param in the last slot of a kernel launch (issue #3202).
+
+        multi_tensor_apply packs at most 36 tensors per launch for depth-4 Adam
+        and 30 for depth-5 Adam with master weights. An empty tensor in the last
+        slot produces no chunks, so it must not keep the following tensors from
+        starting a new launch.
+
+        """
+        if master_weights and not is_bf16_available():
+            pytest.skip("BF16 is not supported")
+        max_tensors_per_launch = 30 if master_weights else 36
+        param_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if master_weights else torch.float32
+        numels = [64] * (max_tensors_per_launch - 1) + [0] + [64] * 20
+
+        # FP32 reference starts from the same (possibly BF16-rounded) values
+        tst_params = [
+            torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(n, device="cuda").to(param_dtype)) for n in numels
+        ]
+        ref_params = [torch.nn.Parameter(p.detach().float()) for p in tst_params]
+        ref_optim = torch.optim.Adam(ref_params, **self.options)
+        tst_optim = self.fused_optim(
+            tst_params, capturable=capturable, master_weights=master_weights, **self.options
+        )
+
+        for _ in range(self.iters):
+            for p_ref, p_tst in zip(ref_params, tst_params):
+                p_tst.grad = torch.randn_like(p_tst)
+                p_ref.grad = p_tst.grad.float()
+            ref_optim.step()
+            tst_optim.step()
+
+        if master_weights:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                [tst_optim.get_unscaled_state(p, "master_param") for p in tst_params],
+                [p.detach() for p in ref_params],
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                [p.detach() for p in tst_params],
+                [p.detach().to(param_dtype) for p in ref_params],
+            )
+        else:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(tst_params, ref_params)
